items.followUp: State two contributions of Al-Jahiz to biology.

rubric.why: Identifies Jabir bin Hayan’s use of experimentation in scientific research.
rubric.description: Introduced the experimental method in scientific research.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he introduced or used the experimental method in scientific research.

rubric.why: Identifies his writing about plants and animals.
rubric.description: Wrote a book about plants and animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a book or writing about both plants and animals.

modelAnswer: Jabir bin Hayan introduced the experimental method in scientific research.
He wrote a book about plants and animals.

rubric.why: Defines diffusion as net movement from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.description: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that molecules move from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: Distinguishes facilitated diffusion by the involvement of membrane proteins while movement is down the gradient.
rubric.description: Facilitated diffusion is movement down the concentration gradient with the help of membrane proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that membrane proteins assist movement down the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Facilitated diffusion is movement down the concentration gradient across a membrane with the help of membrane proteins.

items.followUp: What are the two main stages of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: Defines the cell cycle as the sequence of events between cell divisions.
rubric.description: The cell cycle is the series of events in a cell from one division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the cell cycle as the events occurring from one cell division to the next.

rubric.why: Names both major phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.description: The two major phases are interphase and the division (M) phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both interphase and the division or M phase.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events in a cell from one cell division to the next.
Its two major phases are interphase and the division (M) phase.

items.followUp: What is autolysis, and how can lysosomes bring it about?

rubric.why: Identifies rupture of lysosomes and release of their digestive enzymes.
rubric.description: Lysosomes rupture and release digestive enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomes rupture or burst and release enzymes.

rubric.why: Explains that the released enzymes digest cell material and cause cell destruction or death.
rubric.description: The enzymes digest cell components, causing cell destruction and death.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking digestion of cell components with cell destruction or death.

modelAnswer: During necrosis, lysosomes may rupture and release digestive enzymes.
These enzymes digest cell components, causing cell destruction and death.
